answer: One-time pigment stamp registry. A licensed issuer gives each vetted adult a pad whose microdot ink code is unique; on first redemption the code burns on-chain, with a liveness selfie hash as the anchor and the pad serial recorded, so a clone can never redeem it twice. Farming 1,000 accounts costs 1,000 real identities, $85 each in issuer fees, 2.5 hours per counter visit, and $40 of USDC for liveness compute — about $125,000 and 250 office hours. Every account enters through one narrow inlet: a human at a counter. Picture a passport office burning each ink sheet after one use.
